data_notes:
PERSISTENCE SLICE — no persistent entities, no tables, no repositories.

Finding: this feature ("Honour the PORT environment variable") is a process-startup configuration change confined to `src/index.ts` (currently `const PORT = 3000;` passed to `app.listen({ port: PORT, host: '0.0.0.0' })`, with the log line `Server is running on http://localhost:${PORT}`). It reads one environment variable, computes an integer, and passes it to the HTTP listener. It creates, reads, updates, or deletes no domain state.

Consequences for this slice:
- sqlSchemas: EMPTY. No new table, no column, no index, and no migration is required. Inventing a table (e.g. a `server_config` / `app_settings` row holding the port) would contradict the feature's stated contract — the port comes from the environment, not from the database — and would add a DB dependency to process startup, which currently has none. The existing conceptual tables (employees, leave_types, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, notifications, audit_logs) are unchanged and are already specified once in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; they are not restated here.
- repositories: EMPTY. No repository interface and therefore no concrete implementation. GP-001 (all DB access through repositories) is not engaged because there is no DB access. The existing `IEmployeeRepository`/`PgEmployeeRepository`, `ILeaveRepository`/`PgLeaveRequestRepository`, `IBalanceRepository`/`PgLeaveBalanceRepository`, `IPolicyRepository`/`PgLeavePolicyRepository`, `ILeaveTypeRepository`/`PgLeaveTypeRepository`, `IAuditRepository`/`PgAuditLogRepository`, and `INotificationRepository`/`PgNotificationRepository` (all PostgreSQL via the shared `pg` Pool in `src/shared/db/connection.ts`) are untouched.
- transactionContract: EMPTY, deliberately. There are zero writes, so there is no multi-step write to make atomic and no unit of work to own. The existing contract (service-owned `IUnitOfWork.withTransaction`; repositories accept an optional trailing `PoolClient` defaulting to the shared pool) is unaffected and must not be extended to cover startup.
- GP-002 (audit records): not engaged — no state-changing domain operation. A port value is not domain state and must not be written to `audit_logs`.
- GP-003 (input validation): engaged at the process boundary, not the API boundary. The PORT value is untrusted input and must be validated before use; the validation rule is the open question recorded below.
- GP-004 (no sensitive data in logs): the existing startup log line is retained and must stay accurate for whichever port is actually used. It logs only the port — no secret, no PII — so it remains compliant. Note the log currently prints `http://localhost:${PORT}` while the listener binds `0.0.0.0`; that pre-existing inaccuracy is out of scope for this feature and is not a persistence concern.
- GP-007 (UUIDs in external interfaces): not engaged — no identifier is exposed.

Consistency with docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: this feature adds no module, no dependency edge, and no cross-cutting contract. It does not contradict any recorded decision. It is orthogonal to the modular-monolith module map (shared-types, shared-db, shared-errors, shared-date, shared-auth, employee, leave-type, policy, audit, notification, balance, validation, leave) and to the web build under `web/src/`. If the port resolution is extracted into a helper (see open question 2), the natural home is a new `src/shared/config/` entry point or a module-local helper in `src/index.ts`; either way it must not import from any domain module, and it must not be placed in `src/shared/db/` since it has nothing to do with the database.

Two open questions are recorded (the canonical positive-integer parse rule, and where the resolution lives so the required unit test can exercise all three cases). Both are genuinely undecided and both are binding across the runtime read and the test's expectations; neither can be settled by asserting a value in one call site.

open_questions.question: What exactly counts as a "positive integer" PORT value — i.e. which parsing rule is canonical for the fallback decision? The feature says fall back to 3000 when PORT is "unset or not a positive integer", but the parse rule is not fixed and must hold identically in src/index.ts and in the new unit test.
open_questions.impact: This is the feature's only foundational semantic (the analogue of a day-count/rounding rule): it is binding across the runtime read in src/index.ts and the test's expectations. If the implementation uses parseInt/Number coercion, values like '3000abc', '3000.5', ' 3000 ', '0xBB8', '1e3', '+3000' and '-1' resolve differently than under a strict /^[1-9][0-9]*$/ check, so the test and the runtime can disagree and the "falls back to 3000" contract becomes ambiguous. It also determines whether PORT=0 (ephemeral port) is honoured or rejected, and whether an out-of-range value (e.g. 70000) is rejected.
candidate_options: Strict: accept only a string matching /^[1-9][0-9]*$/ (no sign, no whitespace, no decimals, no trailing junk) and within 1..65535; everything else falls back to 3000
Number(value) + Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 (accepts ' 3000 ' and '1e3', rejects '3000abc' and '3000.5'); no upper bound
parseInt(value, 10) + Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 (accepts '3000abc' as 3000, rejects '3000.5' as 3000 is returned... actually parseInt('3000.5') = 3000, so it accepts it); no upper bound
Strict positive-integer check plus an explicit 1..65535 range guard, treating out-of-range as invalid and falling back to 3000

open_questions.question: Where does the port resolution live so the required unit test can exercise all three cases? src/index.ts currently calls start() at module import time (a side effect), so importing it in Jest would bind a real socket and make the "PORT unset / valid / non-numeric" cases untestable as written.
open_questions.impact: Determines whether the feature is testable at all without a live listener, and whether the startup log line stays accurate. If the resolution stays inline in src/index.ts, the test must either mock app.listen and the module side effect or spawn a child process; if it is extracted, the test is a pure function test. This is a design decision the persistence slice cannot make, but it gates the feature's stated acceptance criterion (a unit test covering the three cases).
candidate_options: Extract a pure resolvePort(env) helper (e.g. src/config/port.ts or src/shared/config) and have src/index.ts call it; unit-test the helper directly with no server boot
Keep the logic inline in src/index.ts and test it by mocking app.listen plus the module import side effect (jest.isolateModules / jest.mock('./app'))
Keep the logic inline and test it end-to-end by spawning src/index.ts as a child process with different PORT values and asserting the bound port / log line
Extract the helper AND guard the start() call behind a require.main === module check so importing the module in tests has no side effect
